source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reserve seat-belt use mainly for highway travel because short local trips have minimal serious-injury risk.","B":"Adults seated in the rear seat can omit seat belts when the vehicle has front and side airbags.","C":"Wear a seat belt on every trip because consistent restraint use substantially reduces the risk of serious crash-related injury or death.","D":"Seat belts are primarily a pediatric intervention and add little protection after a passenger reaches adulthood."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC states that seat belts are the most effective way to prevent injury or death in crashes for adults and older children and that they reduce serious crash-related injuries and deaths by about half. Consistent use on every trip is recommended.
source_row.source_detail: Seat belts reduce serious crash-related injuries and deaths and should be used on every trip. CDC page dated 2026-01-27; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
